title: Why Modern EV Batteries Are Still Expensive: The Cathode Choke
hook: For a decade, the auto industry promised that hundred-dollar battery packs would make electric cars cheaper than gasoline. But that curve just hit an impenetrable wall.

scenes.narration: Between 2010 and 2020, battery costs plummeted by nearly ninety percent. But today, average electric vehicle battery packs have stalled out near one hundred and thirty-nine dollars per kilowatt hour.
scenes.purpose: Establish the stubborn battery pack price plateau at 139 dollars per kilowatt hour
scenes.visual_hint: Statistic card showing $139/kWh average pack cost plateau curve

scenes.narration: The reason isn't factory inefficiency. Gigafactories are more automated than ever. The trap is that raw cathode minerals have surged from forty percent to over seventy-two percent of total cell costs.
scenes.purpose: Contrast manufacturing labor overhead against raw mineral domination at 72 percent
scenes.visual_hint: Comparison breakdown showing bill of materials shift from 40% to 72% raw precursors

scenes.narration: From the eleven-hundred dollar compliance cars of 2010 to the mass market inflection of 2020, price cuts came easy. But as spot mineral markets erupted, the low-hanging fruit completely evaporated.
scenes.purpose: Trace the historic cost curve from 1100 dollars down to the current inflection
scenes.visual_hint: Milestone timeline tracking battery cost deflation and the commodity inflection point

scenes.narration: Compounding the chemical cost, China controls seventy-five percent of global lithium chemical refining and eighty-five percent of synthetic graphite. Building localized supply chains carries a massive capital penalty.
scenes.purpose: Expose the geographic refining choke point controlling 75 percent of precursor chemicals
scenes.visual_hint: Technical schematic detailing the precursor refining bottleneck and international tariff walls

scenes.narration: Until solid-state chemistry achieves mass automotive yields in the late 2020s, the battery remains less like consumer electronics, and more like an expensive refined industrial asset.
scenes.purpose: Synthesize the thermodynamic floor and conclude with the future outlook
scenes.visual_hint: Kinetic typography framing the chemical cost reality of the clean energy transition

ending: The electric vehicle revolution will not be won by software. It will be decided in the chemistry of the cathode.
